name: Workbench P-001 native Windows portable fixture regression
summary: Previously executed native Windows main PUI test target after portable fixture repair: 1393 passed, 0 failed, 19 ignored in 30.77s. The seven formerly failing cases separately passed in 8.70s. This imports retained execution evidence; no suite was replayed. These are test executable results, not installed-app acceptance or shipment proof. Five other Windows test targets and native installed Ubuntu/macOS/Windows acceptance remain outside this evidence.

rootCause: Unix-only absolute-path and PATH fixtures, runtime reads of an unavailable compile-time Linux source tree, and missing real Git in the native VM. The detector gap was lack of actual Windows execution: prior Linux and cross-compilation checks could not exercise these OS assumptions.
recurrenceGuard: The existing seven maintained Cargo tests now run with portable fixtures and embedded source snapshots. Their native Windows execution, including real Git, checks the same failure classes without skipping or quarantining tests.
